The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a key parameter in determining the force's magnitude.

Friction force is also influenced by the coefficient of friction, which varies depending on the surface material and the normal force acting on the pendulum, normal force being a critical factor in determining the friction coefficient.

Coefficient of friction is affected by the surface roughness and the presence of any lubricants, surface roughness being a significant factor in determining the friction coefficient.

Surface roughness can also be influenced by the temperature and humidity of the environment, temperature being a key factor in determining the surface roughness.

Temperature can also affect the viscosity of the lubricant, viscosity being a critical parameter in determining the friction coefficient.

Viscosity is influenced by the type of lubricant used and the surface roughness of the pendulum, type of lubricant being a key factor in determining the viscosity.

Type of lubricant can also be affected by the temperature and humidity of the environment, temperature being a critical factor in determining the type of lubricant.

In the physical pendulum model, the viscous friction force should be taken into account when the pendulum is subject to high velocities or when the surface is rough, high velocities being a key factor in determining the need for friction consideration.

High velocities can also occur when the pendulum is subjected to external forces or when it is in a high-speed environment, external forces being a critical factor in determining the need for friction consideration.

External forces can also be influenced by the mass and moment of inertia of the pendulum, mass being a key parameter in determining the external forces acting on the pendulum.

Mass is also affected by the gravitational acceleration and the surface gravity, gravitational acceleration being a critical factor in determining the mass of the pendulum.

Gravitational acceleration can also be influenced by the latitude and altitude of the location, latitude being a key factor in determining the gravitational acceleration.

Latitude can also be affected by the time of year and the Earth's slightly ellipsoidal shape, time of year being a critical factor in determining the latitude.

Time of year can also be influenced by the Earth's axial tilt and the solar radiation, axial tilt being a key factor in determining the time of year.

Slightly ellipsoidal shape can also be affected by the Earth's slightly oblate spheroid shape and the solar radiation, oblate spheroid shape being a critical factor in determining the slightly ellipsoidal shape.
